title: Oncall handoff and SLO walkthrough — ops prep
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal prep notes for the weekly SRE ops sync. Focus areas: current SLO posture, recent paging trends, top 3 incidents (last 30d), and items to raise with infra/product. This is a scratchpad — keep rough.

TL;DR (for standup):
- SLOs: infra-read/write availability at 99.97% last 30d (target 99.99%) — 2 regressions linked to cache eviction bug and regional infra flakiness.
- Paging: average pages per day (team) = 3.1, notice increase in late-night pages (00:00–04:00 UTC) — likely region failover alignment.
- Top incidents: INC-2248 (cache thrash), OPS-3421 (redis failover miscoord), short tail of high-latency spikes tied to model onboarding jobs.

Agenda (my flow):
1) Quick numbers + signal check (30s) — bring the SLO deltas and paging heatmap
2) Deep dive request: INC-2248 root cause summary and mitigation progress (2–3min)
3) Discuss night-time paging trend and routing/fallback policy tweak options (2min)
4) Follow-ups / owners + canary changes for model-onboarding pipeline (1min)
5) AOB — reminders for runbooks and handoff checklist updates

Data points to have on hand (prep):
- SLO summary table (30d / 7d / 24h): availability, p99 latency, error rate. I'll paste the numbers in meeting: 30d availability 99.97% (-0.02% vs target), 7d 99.95% (-0.04%), 24h 99.92% (-0.07%).
- Pages by time bucket (local): 00–04 UTC: 38% of pages, peak at 02:10 UTC (last week)
- Top alert noise sources (last 14d): cache svc (22%), Redis failovers (18%), inference-gateway 5xx (15%)

Notes on Top Incidents (short):
- INC-2248 — cache thrash (2026-07-03)
  - Symptom: sudden surge of cache-miss storms when KV-cache TTLs expired concurrently after deployment. Amplified by concurrent re-pop requests.
  - Root cause (current): race in cache-warmup hook + bad fallback that retries aggressively instead of using local rate-limit.
  - Mitigations in flight: rate-limit fallback in gateway (PR #5678), staggered TTL rollout script (ops-scripts repo), temporary throttling rule in front proxy.
  - Next: validate PR on staging canary, add slow rollout plan to Dedicated clusters, add metrics for cache-warmup concurrency.

- OPS-3421 — redis failover miscoord (2026-06-29, recurring blips)
  - Symptom: split-brain leading to transient write loss; clients retried, causing spikes in 5xx and downstream backpressure.
  - Root cause: older Redis version + misconfigured sentinel timeouts in one region; failovers took too long and triggered retries.
  - Work: infra patch scheduled (upgrade to 6.2.10) + sentinel tuning; cross-region fallback tested but needs more canary traffic.
  - Owner: Riley C. (infra) — need timeline in this week's sync.

Paging trends + hypotheses:
- Night-window pages higher because some customers route traffic to nearest region and region B rotates maintenance at 00:00 UTC. Also model-onboarding jobs (automated quantization) run at odd hours and can saturate KV caches.
- Hypotheses to test:
  1) Onboarding job schedule collides with TTL expirations (offset jobs by 3h)
  2) Fallback policy triggers too eagerly — consider increasing local-circuit threshold
  3) Alerting thresholds are too sensitive for transient post-deploy flaps (tweak for deploy-tagged incidents)

Runbook / playbook gaps I've noticed (notes to self):
- cache-thrash playbook needs a clear immediate mitigation: how to flip to degraded-mode (serve stale while healing) — add steps & safe toggles
- redis failover runbook: add explicit sentinel timeout table + how to rollback sentinel config change
- onboarding pipeline: add a "pause new onboards" kill switch for when gateways show >5% 5xx anomaly

Action items (who/what/due):
- Morgan D.: paste final SLO table into sync deck and update heatmap (by EOD 2026-07-11) [DONE draft — finalize after infra ETA]
- Riley C.: confirm Redis upgrade window and expected disruption (due 2026-07-13)
- Aisha B.: validate cache-warmup concurrency metrics instrumentation PR (PR #5684) and flag any visibility gaps (due 2026-07-12)
- Product: consider shifting non-urgent onboarding jobs to UTC business hours (ask PM @alex to weigh in) (ask in meeting)
- Ops-scripts: implement staggered TTL rollout script and add to canary pipeline (owner: ops-scripts team) (due 2026-07-19)

Meeting talking points / phrasing (copy/paste-able):
- "Short signal: we're 0.02–0.07% under SLO on 30/7/1 day windows driven by cache thrash and region failovers — both have mitigations but need timeline commitment to avoid repeat."
- "Immediate ask: Riley — what's the ETA on the Redis upgrade and do you expect <1h downtime or rolling no-downtime? We'll map customer impact and adjust oncall rota if needed."
- "Operational change proposal: stagger TTLs and add a temporary "serve stale" toggle in gateway to reduce churn on cache storms. We can remove after two weeks if stable."

Handoff checklist (for oncall):
- ensure runbooks linked in pager message
- escalate to infra channel if Redis upgrade intersects oncall window
- if cache-thrash observed: flip proxy throttle and open INC-xxxx with "cache-thrash" template
- check metrics dashboard: cache hit-rate, backend p95 latency, open bags in tracing for request fanout

Questions / unresolved:
- can product confirm the set of customers affected by the cache failover? (need to know whether it's a small tenant vector or broad)
- how tightly coupled are onboarding jobs to model catalog updates? Could we gate them behind a manual approval for first 24h?

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep this doc informal — use it to riff in meeting. Capture any new owners and paste into next week's formal SLO review doc.
- After sync: follow up on PRs, update runbook drafts, and schedule a deep-dive (30m) with infra if Redis upgrade window >1 day.
- remember to cc support lead (Nadia K.) if customer-impacting windows are >30m so CS can pre-notify big accounts.

Links to paste in chat quickly:
- SLO defs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/1598/SLO+Definitions
- INC-2248: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2248
- OPS-3421: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-3421

End of scratchpad.

-- Morgan
